text: If today you were to freely choose a spiritual path for your life without any pressure, why should you consider Islam? The answer I'm sharing with you in this section is clear. In my view, Islam possesses advantages that make it worthy of attention and choice. But let me clarify one thing right from the beginning. When I say I prefer Islam, it does not mean I consider other paths invalid or worthless. In my belief, what shapes human destiny prior to any name or title is truth-seeking, inner purity, and morality. Any human being, religious or non-religious, who sincerely seeks truth and goodness is not entirely barred from the path. Nevertheless, spirituality is not something that remains solely in the mind. For it to take root in life, it needs a clear path, a practical method. And the question is, among the paths opened throughout human history to connect with God, which one is clearer, more rational, and closer to our innate nature, fitra? I share my reasons honestly with you while at the same time respecting those who have chosen a different path based on their own reasons. The right way is to listen to the arguments and choose whichever we find more convincing. But let me say right from the start that my reason is not that the era of other religions has passed and they have all been rendered void. I make no such claim. Interestingly, the Quran itself does not say this either. The Quran does not declare past divine religions and scriptures such as the Torah and the Gospel as void. Rather, it confirms them and considers itself the continuation and completion of that very same path. The Quran states that for the same reason those books came from God, this book is also from God. That means Islam does not need to belittle the paths of others to prove itself. It sees itself as the final link in a continuous chain. And precisely right here forms one of the most reasons. If we accept that these heavenly messages throughout history have been a continuous and evolving sequence moving toward perfection, then it is entirely rational to pay special attention to the last and most complete message in this chain. This is the same thing we do every day in life. When faced with a series of successive versions, we select the latest and most complete one. Even on our phones, we strive to use the latest version of every app because we know it includes the newest refinements and best features. Another reason is that in Islam we have access to the most reliable source of this message. The text of the Quran in the exact words in which it was originally expressed has reached us intact. And this gives us confidence that what we read is the original message itself, not an altered account over the passage of centuries. But perhaps the most important thing that convinces me is the position of wisdom and intellect in this religion. While it is true that all religions call people to knowledge and wisdom, few books place such emphasis on thinking, on intellect, and on the value of knowledge as the Quran does. The Quran continuously asks humans not to accept anything without understanding, and it censures blind imitation. For someone whose standard is intellect and innate nature, a religion that values wisdom to this extent is naturally closer and more acceptable. This very rationalism manifests itself in the most paramount matter, theology, knowing God. The picture the Quran presents of God is simple and clear, requiring no complex justifications. One, peerless God who resembles none of his creations. And perhaps the most beautiful part of the matter is that one can approach this God directly without an intermediary. In Islam, to speak with God, to turn back and repent, you need no intermediary person or institution. Anyone at any time can speak directly to him. God feels closer in this religion, as close as an inner whisper. And this feeling of closeness is for many a discovery in itself. There are other advantages that can be enumerated following these. The balance it establishes between this world and the hereafter, neither despising material life nor sacrificing spirituality for it. Its emphasis on justice and its respect for freedom of belief and freedom of choosing a religion. The very freedom that gives you the right to reflect calmly without compulsion and decide for yourself. I do not invite you to a hasty acceptance. I invite you to reflect. If what I have said opened a new window before you, my suggestion is that you go directly to the Quran yourself and encounter it without intermediaries. Let it speak to you directly. And if you have any questions or doubts along this journey, I will gladly stand by your side and answer them.
